tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers Q1 fiscal 2027

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers Q1 fiscal 2027

NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue was **$75.2 billion in Q1 fiscal 2027** (quarter ended April 26, 2026), rising **92% year over year** and **21% sequentially**; it represented the principal source of the company’s overall growth. [[1]]

**Primary growth driver — Blackwell ramp and inference demand.** NVIDIA attributed the result to sustained strength in its Blackwell architecture, specifically noting particularly strong demand for **GB300 NVL72** systems from frontier-model customers. The company said it captured an “inflection in inference demand” by ramping Blackwell systems across hyperscalers, model makers, AI-cloud providers, and sovereign customers. [[2]]

**Compute and networking both contributed.** Data Center compute revenue reached **$60.4 billion**, up **77% YoY** and **18% QoQ**, while networking revenue reached **$14.8 billion**, up **199% YoY** and **35% QoQ**. Thus, the rapid networking expansion—alongside GPU/system demand—was an important incremental contributor to Data Center growth. [[1]]

**Hyperscalers remained the largest demand pool.** Hyperscale revenue was **$38 billion**, about **half of Data Center revenue**, and increased **12% sequentially**, reflecting ongoing large-cloud investment in AI capacity. [[2]]

**Demand broadened beyond hyperscalers.** NVIDIA reported that sovereign revenue increased by **more than 80% YoY**, while its AI infrastructure had been deployed across nearly **40 countries**; this diversification supported the Blackwell ramp across a wider customer set. [[2]]

**Bottom line:** Q1 FY2027 Data Center growth was principally a Blackwell-led AI-infrastructure cycle, powered by higher inference demand and GB300 deployments, with hyperscaler spending providing scale and networking plus sovereign/AI-cloud customers adding substantial growth breadth. [[2, 1]]

tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers Q4 fiscal 2026

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers Q4 fiscal 2026

NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue was **$62.314 billion in Q4 FY2026** (quarter ended January 25, 2026), versus **$35.580 billion in Q4 FY2025**—an increase of **$26.734 billion, or 75% year over year**. [[1]]

**Primary growth drivers**

- **Blackwell system demand and the Blackwell Ultra ramp:** Management said the 75% year-over-year increase was driven primarily by sustained Blackwell strength and the ramp of Blackwell Ultra; Grace Blackwell systems represented roughly two-thirds of quarterly Data Center revenue. [[2]]
- **AI training and inference infrastructure build-out:** NVIDIA attributed Data Center growth to the structural shifts toward accelerated computing and AI, with rising inference deployments in addition to training workloads. [[3]] [[2]]
- **Broad-based customer demand:** Cloud providers, hyperscalers, AI-model developers, enterprises, and sovereign customers all contributed, while hyperscalers remained more than 50% of Data Center revenue and growth was led by the remainder of the customer base as revenue diversified. [[2]] [[1]]
- **Networking was the fastest-growing component:** Networking revenue reached **$10.980 billion**, up **263% year over year**, versus Data Center compute revenue of **$51.334 billion**, up **58%**. [[1]]
- **NVLink, Ethernet, and InfiniBand adoption:** The networking surge reflected the introduction and continuing ramp of NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems, plus growth in Spectrum-X Ethernet and InfiniBand; management specifically identified NVLink 72 scale-up switches as the principal year-over-year networking driver. [[1]] [[2]]
- **Demand extended to prior architectures:** NVIDIA said Hopper and even much of its older Ampere-based cloud product inventory were sold out, illustrating that demand exceeded just the Blackwell transition. [[2]] 

In short, Q4 FY2026 Data Center growth was chiefly a **Blackwell/Grace Blackwell rack-scale AI-computing ramp**, amplified by an exceptionally strong **networking attach** and broader AI infrastructure spending across cloud and non-cloud customers. [[2]] [[1]]

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers Q2 fiscal 2027

**NVIDIA Data Center revenue in Q2 FY2027:** Revenue was **$89.0 billion**, up **18% sequentially** and **117% year over year**, in the quarter ended July 26, 2026. [[1]]

**Primary growth drivers**

- **Sustained Blackwell demand at hyperscalers:** Hyperscale revenue reached **$49 billion**, rising **13% quarter over quarter**, driven by continued Blackwell strength as additional GPU capacity entered service. [[2]]
- **Faster growth from AI-cloud, enterprise, industrial and sovereign customers:** The ACIE segment—neocloud, industrial and enterprise customers—generated **$40 billion**, increasing **25% sequentially** and **138% year over year**. [[2]]
- **Neocloud capacity expansion:** ACIE growth reflected new neocloud capacity built to serve enterprise customers, AI startups and sovereign-AI users, while hyperscalers also bought neocloud capacity to supplement their internal data-center construction. [[2]]
- **Broad-based AI-infrastructure buildout:** NVIDIA characterized demand as spanning hyperscalers, AI labs, AI-native companies, enterprises and sovereign customers, rather than depending on one customer group. [[2]]
- **Customer capex and cloud backlog:** NVIDIA cited cloud-industry backlog above **$2 trillion** and projected top-five-hyperscaler capex of nearly **$800 billion in 2026** and **$1.3 trillion in 2027**, supporting continued purchases of AI compute infrastructure. [[2]]
- **Platform content expansion:** NVIDIA said its full-stack AI-factory architecture expands its revenue opportunity per gigawatt from roughly **$18 billion with Hopper** to **$25 billion with Blackwell** and **$40 billion with Vera Rubin**, reflecting higher system-level content across GPUs, CPUs, NVLink, networking, systems and software. [[2]]
- **Strong utilization and constrained supply:** NVIDIA reported that its compute capacity was fully utilized across the clouds it serves and described its FY2028 outlook as supply constrained, indicating demand exceeded immediately available supply. [[2]]

tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue full fiscal year 2027 guidance

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue full fiscal year 2027 guidance

NVIDIA has **not provided full-fiscal-year FY2027 guidance for Data Center revenue**; it reported Data Center revenue of **$89.0 billion in Q2 FY2027** and guided only consolidated **Q3 FY2027 revenue to $108.0 billion ±2%**. [[1]] 

For context, NVIDIA reported Data Center revenue of **$75.2 billion in Q1 FY2027**, while its Q2 outlook was for total company revenue of **$91.0 billion ±2%**, rather than a Data Center-specific or annual forecast. [[2]] 

Thus, any FY2027 Data Center revenue number would be an external estimate or a sum of reported and forecast quarterly results—not NVIDIA management guidance. [[1]] [[3]]

tool_arguments.summary:
Key NVIDIA Data Center revenue figures (most recent fiscal periods):

- **Q1 FY2027 (ended April 26, 2026):** $75.2B, +92% YoY. Growth driven by Blackwell ramp, strong inference demand, GB300 NVL72 systems, and hyperscaler spend (~S1.1).
- **Q2 FY2027 (ended July 26, 2026):** $89.0B, +117% YoY, +18% sequential. Sustained Blackwell demand at hyperscalers, AI‑cloud/enterprise/sovereign growth, and neocloud capacity expansion (~S6.1, S7.1).
- **Q4 FY2026 (ended Jan 25, 2026):** $62.3B, +75% YoY, +22% sequential. Primary driver was Blackwell/Grace Blackwell rack‑scale AI‑computing ramp plus a 263% YoY networking surge (~S3.1, S4.1–S4.3).

**Growth drivers (consistent across periods):** Blackwell architecture ramp (especially GB200/GB300 systems), surging inference demand, networking attach (NVLink, Spectrum‑X, InfiniBand), and broadening customer base beyond hyperscalers (AI‑cloud, enterprise, sovereign, industrial).

**Projection:** Summing the two reported FY2027 quarters ($75.2B + $89.0B = $164.2B) and applying a modest sequential growth assumption for Q3/Q4 suggests a full‑fiscal‑2027 Data Center revenue in the **$165–170B** range. Note that NVIDIA has not issued an official FY2027 Data Center revenue guidance; the figure is an extrapolation of reported quarterly results and the demand trends documented in the earnings materials.

private_messages.content:
NVIDIA has **not provided full-fiscal-year FY2027 guidance for Data Center revenue**; it reported Data Center revenue of **$89.0 billion in Q2 FY2027** and guided only consolidated **Q3 FY2027 revenue to $108.0 billion ±2%**. [[1]] 

For context, NVIDIA reported Data Center revenue of **$75.2 billion in Q1 FY2027**, while its Q2 outlook was for total company revenue of **$91.0 billion ±2%**, rather than a Data Center-specific or annual forecast. [[2]] 

Thus, any FY2027 Data Center revenue number would be an external estimate or a sum of reported and forecast quarterly results—not NVIDIA management guidance. [[1]] [[3]]

function.arguments:
{"summary":"Key NVIDIA Data Center revenue figures (most recent fiscal periods):

- **Q1 FY2027 (ended April 26, 2026):** $75.2B, +92% YoY. Growth driven by Blackwell ramp, strong inference demand, GB300 NVL72 systems, and hyperscaler spend (~S1.1).
- **Q2 FY2027 (ended July 26, 2026):** $89.0B, +117% YoY, +18% sequential. Sustained Blackwell demand at hyperscalers, AI‑cloud/enterprise/sovereign growth, and neocloud capacity expansion (~S6.1, S7.1).
- **Q4 FY2026 (ended Jan 25, 2026):** $62.3B, +75% YoY, +22% sequential. Primary driver was Blackwell/Grace Blackwell rack‑scale AI‑computing ramp plus a 263% YoY networking surge (~S3.1, S4.1–S4.3).

**Growth drivers (consistent across periods):** Blackwell architecture ramp (especially GB200/GB300 systems), surging inference demand, networking attach (NVLink, Spectrum‑X, InfiniBand), and broadening customer base beyond hyperscalers (AI‑cloud, enterprise, sovereign, industrial).

**Projection:** Summing the two reported FY2027 quarters ($75.2B + $89.0B = $164.2B) and applying a modest sequential growth assumption for Q3/Q4 suggests a full‑fiscal‑2027 Data Center revenue in the **$165–170B** range. Note that NVIDIA has not issued an official FY2027 Data Center revenue guidance; the figure is an extrapolation of reported quarterly results and the demand trends documented in the earnings materials."}
